'''Thomas Weimbs''' (born in [[Germany]]) is a German-American molecular biologist and cell biologist. He is a professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] (UCSB) and the head of the Weimbs Laboratory.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://labs.mcdb.ucsb.edu/weimbs/thomas |title=Curriculum Vitae Thomas Weimbs, Ph.D. |website=University of California Santa Barbara |date=2026 |access-date=2026-07-09}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Messing |first1=Melina |last2=Torres |first2=Jacob A. |last3=Holznecht |first3=Nickolas |last4=Weimbs |first4=Thomas |title=Trigger Warning: How Modern Diet, Lifestyle, and Environment Pull the Trigger on Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Progression |journal=Nutrients |date=2024 |volume=16 |issue=19 |page=3281 |doi=10.3390/nu16193281 |doi-access=free |pmid=39408247 |pmc=11479178 }}</ref>

== Career ==

Weimbs earned his Diplom Chemiker (MS) in 1990 and his Dr. rer. nat. (Ph.D.) in 1993 from the [[University of Cologne]], Germany, researching the structure of the myelin proteolipid protein and its mutations in [[Pelizaeus–Merzbacher disease|Pelizaeus-Merzbacher Disease]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weimbs |first=Thomas |year=1993 |title=Funktionelle Lokalisation der Cystein-Reste und Untersuchungen zur Membran-Topologie des Myelin-Proteolipidproteins |url=https://katalog.ub.uni-koeln.de/portal/databases/id/uni/titles/id/991015890059706476.html?l=de |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=katalog.ub.uni-koeln.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=WEIMBS Pelizaeus-Merzbacher Disease Leads to Disruption of Myelinogenesis |journal=Biological Chemistry Hoppe-Seyler |volume=371 |issue=2 |pages=1175–1184 |doi=10.1515/bchm3.1990.371.2.1175 |pmid=1708672 |issn=0177-3593}}</ref> He subsequently conducted postdoctoral research at the Department of Anatomy, School of Medicine at the [[University of California, San Francisco]] (UCSF) from 1994 to 1999, studying the role of the SNARE membrane fusion machinery in polarized membrane trafficking in epithelial cells.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Weimbs |first1=Thomas |last2=Low |first2=Seng Hui |last3=Chapin |first3=Steven J. |last4=Mostov |first4=Keith E. |last5=Bucher |first5=Philipp |last6=Hofmann |first6=Kay |date=1997-04-01 |title=A conserved domain is present in different families of |pmid=9096343 |bibcode=1997PNAS...94.3046W }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Low |first1=Seng Hui |last2=Chapin |first2=Steven J. |last3=Wimmer |first3=Christian |last4=Whiteheart |first4=Sidney W. |last5=Kömüves |first5=László G. |last6=Mostov |first6=Keith E. |last7=Weimbs |first7=Thomas |date=1998-06-29 |title=The SNARE Machinery Is Involved in Apical Plasma Membrane Trafficking in MDCK Cells |journal=The Journal of Cell Biology |volume=141 |issue=7 |pages=1503–1513 |doi=10.1083/jcb.141.7.1503 |pmid=9647644 |pmc=2133007 |issn=0021-9525}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Weimbs |first1=Thomas |last2=Mostov |first2=Keith |last3=Hui Low |first3=Seng |last4=Hofmann |first4=Kay |date=December 1998 |title=A model for structural similarity between different SNARE complexes based on sequence relationships |journal=Trends in Cell Biology |volume=8 |issue=7 |pages=260–262 |doi=10.1016/s0962-8924(98)01285-9 |pmid=9714596 |issn=0962-8924}}</ref> In 1999, he became an Assistant Staff member at the Lerner Research Institute of the Cleveland Clinic.<ref name=":0" /> Concurrently, he served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Molecular Medicine at the [[Cleveland Clinic]] Lerner College of Medicine of [[Case Western Reserve University]] from 2004 to 2005.<ref name=":0" /> Weimbs transitioned to the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] (UCSB) in 2005 as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology. He attained the rank of Associate Professor with tenure in 2007 and was appointed as a full Professor in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-18 |title=Thomas Weimbs |url=https://news.ucsb.edu/people/thomas-weimbs |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=The Current |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, Weimbs founded Santa Barbara Nutrients, Inc., where he acts as the President and Chief Scientific Officer.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Muensterman |first1=E |title=Real-world outcomes of managing autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease using a medical food as part of a nutrition and lifestyle program to improve renal and metabolic health |journal=Frontiers in Nutrition |date=2025 |doi=10.3389/fnut.2025.1624639 |volume=12 |article-number=1624639 |doi-access=free |pmid=41648752 |pmc=12869025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Thomas Weimbs: Pioneering PKD Researcher |url=https://santabarbaranutrients.com/pages/thomas-weimbs-phd |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Santa Barbara Nutrients |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==

Initially Weimbs studied intracellular membrane trafficking, mapping the differential localization of [[SNARE protein]]s and syntaxin isoforms in polarized epithelial cells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Low |first1=Seng Hui |title=Differential Localization of Syntaxin Isoforms in Polarized MDCK Cells |journal=Molecular Biology of the Cell |date=1996 |doi=10.1091/mbc.7.12.2007 |volume=7 |issue=12 |pages=2007–2018 |pmid=8970161 |pmc=276046 }}</ref>

His research then transitioned to the underlying molecular mechanisms and potential treatments for [[polycystic kidney disease]] (PKD).<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Weimbs |first1=Thomas |title=Polycystic kidney disease and renal injury repair: common pathways, fluid flow, and the function of polycystin-1 |journal=American Journal of Physiology. Renal Physiology |date=2007 |doi=10.1152/ajprenal.00275.2007 |volume=293 |issue=5 |pages=F1423–F1432 |pmid=17715262 }}</ref> His laboratory identified the abnormal activation of the mTOR and STAT signaling pathways in PKD, establishing parallels between cyst growth and normal renal injury repair processes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shillingford |first1=Jonathan M. |last2=Murcia |first2=Noel S. |last3=Larson |first3=Claire H. |last4=Low |first4=Seng Hui |last5=Hedgepeth |first5=Ryan |last6=Brown |first6=Nicole |last7=Flask |first7=Chris A. |last8=Novick |first8=Andrew C. |last9=Goldfarb Sciences |language=en |volume=103 |issue=14 |pages=5466–5471 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0509694103 |doi-access=free |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=1459378 |pmid=16567633}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Low
